content:
alex: quick question — we're migrating payments-proxy service from ALB to NLB so we can do TLS passthrough. after switching the annotation and creating a TLS listener i'm seeing 502s from the LB healthchecks. do pods need to listen on 443 now or can the app keep listening on 8080 and the NLB decrypt to plaintext for the pod? :thinking:

alex: current svc in staging:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payments-proxy
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: "ip"  # i added this to test
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
```
I also created an AWS NLB listener on 443 with protocol=TLS and attached an ACM cert. healthchecks started failing after that.

marta: tl;dr — depends where TLS terminates. two common setups:
- LB terminates TLS (ACM) and forwards plaintext TCP/HTTP to pods => pods can stay on 8080. target group/protocol must be TCP (or HTTP) and healthcheck should match plaintext.
- TLS passthrough: LB forwards raw TLS to pods => pods must terminate TLS (listen on 443/8443) and TG protocol should be TLS (or use TCP healthchecks).

marta: AWS LB controller behaviour matters: it will create TGs based on service targetPort and targetType. if TG protocol is TLS but your pods speak HTTP, you'll get 502/504.

sam: example terraform we used. note protocol on target group determines whether backend expects TLS:
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_listener" "payments_tls" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.nlb.arn
  port              = "443"
  protocol          = "TLS"
  certificate_arn   = data.aws_acm_certificate.payments.arn
  default_action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.payments.arn
  }
}
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "payments" {
  port        = 8080
  protocol    = "TCP"   # plaintext backend
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    protocol = "TCP"
    port     = "8080"
  }
}
```
If protocol is TLS, backend must do TLS. If protocol is TCP, LB will decrypt and send plaintext.

alex: ok. quick clarifying Qs:
1) do we need a k8s TLS secret in the namespace if LB has ACM?
2) what's the minimal change to get staging healthy quickly so i can validate cert in prod?

marta: 1) no, not for LB-terminating TLS. you only need k8s secrets if pods terminate TLS or if you have an Ingress controller doing TLS.

marta: 2) minimal: switch target group protocol -> TCP and healthcheck -> TCP (port 8080), ensure service annotation target-type=ip so TG points to pod IPs and targetPort stays 8080. this lets LB terminate TLS and forward plaintext to pods.

rui: also watch externalTrafficPolicy. if externalTrafficPolicy=Local and you're using node targets, nodes without pods might fail healthchecks. target-type=ip + Cluster policy is simpler for this flow.

sam: another gotcha — when controller creates TGs it uses the service port to build the TG port mapping. double-check the TG port in the AWS console after you apply. we had an incident where TG port was set to 8443 and pods were on 8080.

infra-bot: terraform plan: infra/staging shows change aws_lb_target_group.payments protocol: "TLS" -> "TCP" (will be applied) :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks everyone — i'll update TG protocol to TCP, set healthcheck to TCP on 8080, add aws-load-balancer-target-type: "ip" annotation, and roll. pinging @eng-platform to eyeball the rollout.

rui: happy to pair for smoke test in ~15 if you want.

alex: will do, starting patch now. cheers :rocket:
